docs.text: HardFOC driver MAX22200 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the Analog Devices MAX22200 octal solenoid and motor driver. It brings the chip up, configures each half-bridge for current or voltage drive with HIT and HOLD levels, switches channels, runs bridges and reads faults, on any MCU with SPI. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that moves bytes over SPI and drives the ENABLE and CMD pins; it does the rest: the two-phase command and data protocol, the power-up sequence, register encoding in milliamps, percent and milliseconds, and fault decoding. Octal serial-controlled solenoid and motor driver MAX22200 Analog Devices (Maxim Integrated) Outputs 8 push-pull half-bridges, 0.2 Ω typical, up to 1 A RMS each; pairs in parallel or as full bridges Drive Current regulation (CDR, integrated current sensing, low side) or voltage regulation (VDR, PWM duty) HIT and HOLD 7-bit HIT and HOLD level and 8-bit HIT time per channel; chopping at 20 kHz to 100 kHz Host interface SPI mode 0 up to 10 MHz (5 MHz daisy-chained); the CMD pin selects command or data Control pins ENABLE, CMD, TRIGA, TRIGB (inputs); FAULT (open-drain output) Supply VM 4.5 V to 36 V; logic inputs switch at 1.2 V and take up to 6 V Package 32-pin TQFN 5 mm × 5 mm, −40 °C to +85 °C; the MAX22200A adds selective fault clear Datasheet (Rev. 1, 3/25) · Product page What you get ¶ One object per chip. MAX22200<YourSpi> takes your port and the board's full-scale current, and runs the datasheet's start-up flow in Initialize() . See API guide . Real units. HIT and HOLD in milliamps (CDR) or percent (VDR), HIT time in milliseconds, converted with the board's RREF and the chip's chopping frequency. See Drive modes . Fast switching. Turning channels on and off is one 8-bit write of the ONCH byte; full-bridge pairs take forward, reverse, brake and Hi-Z. See API guide . Faults by channel. STATUS flags, per-channel OCP, HHF, open-load and plunger-movement flags, selective clear on the MAX22200A and the FAULT pin. See API guide . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class: no virtual calls, no heap, no RTOS dependency. See Porting . Tested without hardware. Host unit tests run the driver against a model of the chip's SPI protocol. See Testing and CI . Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Wire the chip, write the port, pull in a solenoid in about 15 lines. API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: initialise, configure channels, switch them, run bridges, read faults and detect plunger movement. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with Driver standing for max22200::MAX22200<MySpi> and DriverStatus for max22200::DriverStatus . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One MAX22200<SpiType> object per chip. Its calls work at three levels: Level Example Use it for A whole channel ConfigureChannel(ch, ChannelConfig) Bring-up: every CFG_CHx field in one write One setting in real units SetHoldCurrentMa(ch, 120) , SetHitTimeMs(ch, 20) Changing one value of a configured channel Raw registers ReadRegister32(bank, v) , WriteRegister8(bank, v) Anything the helpers do not cover Area Calls Start and stop Initialize() , Deinitialize() , EnableDevice() , DisableDevice() Channels ConfigureChannel() , ConfigureChannelCdr() , ConfigureChannelVdr() , GetChannelConfig() Switching EnableChannel() , DisableChannel() , SetChannelsOn() , SetFullBridgeState() Real units SetHit/HoldCurrentMa() , ...CurrentA() , ...CurrentPercent() , ...DutyPercent() , SetHitTimeMs() STATUS ReadStatus() , WriteStatus() Faults ReadFaultRegister() , ClearChannelFaults() , ClearAllFaults() , GetFaultPinState() DPM ConfigureDpm() , SetDpmEnabledChannels() , ReadDpmConfig() , WriteDpmConfig() Every call that reaches the chip returns DriverStatus and never throws. Check it: anything but OK means the value was rejected or the transfer failed ( Architecture ). Initialise ¶ Driver driver ( spi ); driver . SetBoardConfig ( max22200 :: BoardConfig ( 15.0f , false )); // RREF 15 kOhm: IFS = 1000 mA const DriverStatus st = driver . Initialize (); if ( st != DriverStatus :: OK ) { // INITIALIZATION_ERROR: Initialize() or Configure() of the port failed. // COMMUNICATION_ERROR: a transfer failed, or the chip answered COMER three times. std :: printf ( "MAX22200 init failed: %d 
 " , static_cast < int > ( st )); return false ; } Initialize() follows the datasheet's programming flow (Figure 6): it calls your port's Initialize() and Configure(10 MHz, mode 0, MSB first) , raises ENABLE, waits 0.5 ms, reads STATUS to clear the power-up UVM flag, writes STATUS with ACTIVE = 1, every channel off and COMER masked (other masks and pair modes as read: their reset values after power-up), then reads STATUS again. A COMER reply restarts the sequence, up to three times. Set the board's full-scale current before you configure a CDR channel. BoardConfig() without arguments assumes 1000 mA (RREF = 15 kΩ); a wrong IFS scales every current by the same error. The outputs need 2.5 ms (t WU ) after Initialize() before they switch. Deinitialize() , also called by the destructor, turns every channel off, clears ACTIVE and lowers ENABLE. Configure a channel ¶ Configure in this order: pair modes in STATUS (if any), then each channel, then switch channels on. Drive mode and side change only while every channel is off. Current drive (CDR) Voltage drive (VDR) max22200 :: ChannelConfig cfg ; // defaults: CDR, low side, FMAIN_DIV4, all checks off cfg . drive_mode = max22200 :: DriveMode :: CDR ; cfg . side_mode = max22200 :: SideMode :: LOW_SIDE ; cfg . hit_setpoint = 600.0f ; // mA, peak current during the HIT time cfg . hold_setpoint = 200.0f ; // mA, after the HIT time cfg . hit_time_ms = 30.0f ; // rounded to a multiple of 40 / fCHOP cfg . chop_freq = max22200 :: ChopFreq :: FMAIN_DIV4 ; // 25 kHz with FREQM = 0 cfg . hit_current_check_enabled = true ; // HHF flag if 600 mA is not reached in 30 ms cfg . open_load_detection_enabled = true ; // OLF flag if the coil is disconnected if ( driver . ConfigureChannel ( 0 , cfg ) != DriverStatus :: OK ) { return false ; // INVALID_PARAMETER: channel > 7, IFS = 0, or SRC above 50 kHz } // High-side load (to GND): VDR only. Setpoints are duty cycle; see the note on VDR scaling. auto cfg = max22200 :: ChannelConfig :: makeSolenoidVdr ( 100.0f , 40.0f , 50.0f ); cfg . side_mode = max22200 :: SideMode :: HIGH_SIDE ; if ( driver . ConfigureChannel ( 1 , cfg ) != DriverStatus :: OK ) { return false ; } max22200 :: DutyLimits limits ; // deltaMIN / deltaMAX for this channel's fCHOP and SRC if ( driver . GetDutyLimits ( 1 , limits ) == DriverStatus :: OK ) { std :: printf ( "duty %u..%u %% 
 " , limits . min_percent , limits . max_percent ); } ChannelConfig holds every CFG_CHx field; Configuration lists them. The presets makeSolenoidCdr(hit_ma, hold_ma, hit_ms) and makeSolenoidVdr(hit_pct, hold_pct, hit_ms) fill a low-side channel at FMAIN_DIV4 ; ConfigureChannelCdr() and ConfigureChannelVdr() do the same in one call with the other fields as arguments. VDR percentages The driver scales VDR duty by 127 / 100 before writing it, but the chip reads the field as percent: 40 % runs at 51 %. Drive modes explains it and the workaround. Switch channels ¶ // Each call is one 8-bit write of STATUS[31:24] (ONCH): two short SPI transfers. if ( driver . EnableChannel ( 0 ) != DriverStatus :: OK ) return false ; if ( driver . SetChannelsOn ( 0b0000'0101 ) != DriverStatus :: OK ) return false ; // channels 0 and 2 on if ( driver . DisableAllChannels () != DriverStatus :: OK ) return false ; All switching writes STATUS[31:24], the ONCH byte, with an 8-bit access. The driver keeps the last ONCH value, so EnableChannel(2) leaves the other channels as they were. A channel whose trigger_from_pin is set follows its TRIG pin instead of ONCH. Change a setting while running ¶ // Change one setting of a running channel: read-modify-write of CFG_CH0 in real units. if ( driver . SetHoldCurrentMa ( 0 , 120 ) != DriverStatus :: OK ) return false ; uint32_t hold_ma = 0 ; if ( driver . GetHoldCurrentMa ( 0 , hold_ma ) == DriverStatus :: OK ) { std :: printf ( "hold %lu mA 
 " , static_cast < unsigned long > ( hold_ma )); // quantised to IFS / 127 } Each Set...() call reads CFG_CHx, changes one field and writes all 32 bits back. HOLD current, chopping frequency and SRC can change while the channel is on; drive mode and side cannot. The ...A() variants take amperes, the ...CurrentPercent() variants a fraction of IFS. The current setters also set the channel to CDR and the duty setters to VDR: use each only on a channel already in that mode, or the other setpoint is reinterpreted in the wrong unit. Run a full bridge ¶ // Channels 2 and 3 as one full bridge (a brushed DC motor or a latching valve). // Change CMxy only while both channels are off. max22200 :: StatusConfig status ; if ( driver . ReadStatus ( status ) != DriverStatus :: OK ) return false ; status . channels_on_mask &= static_cast < uint8_t > ( ~ 0b0000'1100 ); status . channel_pair_mode_32 = max22200 :: ChannelMode :: HBRIDGE ; if ( driver . WriteStatus ( status ) != DriverStatus :: OK ) return false ; // Forward runs from CFG_CH3, reverse from CFG_CH2 (datasheet Table 7). if ( driver . ConfigureChannelCdr ( 3 , 500 , 300 , 10.0f ) != DriverStatus :: OK ) return false ; if ( driver . ConfigureChannelCdr ( 2 , 500 , 300 , 10.0f ) != DriverStatus :: OK ) return false ; const uint8_t pair = 1 ; // 0: CH0/CH1, 1: CH2/CH3, 2: CH4/CH5, 3: CH6/CH7 if ( driver . SetFullBridgeState ( pair , max22200 :: FullBridgeState :: Forward ) != DriverStatus :: OK ) return false ; return driver . SetFullBridgeState ( pair , max22200 :: FullBridgeState :: Brake ) == DriverStatus :: OK ; FullBridgeState OUTx / OUTy Settings from HiZ (ONCHy = 0, ONCHx = 0) Hi-Z / Hi-Z Forward (0, 1) VM / regulated CFG_CHy Reverse (1, 0) regulated / VM CFG_CHx Brake (1, 1) GND / GND x is the even channel of the pair, y the odd one. In PARALLEL mode the even channel's configuration drives both outputs and the odd channel's is ignored; switch both channels on together. Handle faults ¶ bool pin_active = false ; // FAULT pin, read through the port driver . GetFaultPinState ( pin_active ); max22200 :: StatusConfig status ; // global flags; reading clears UVM and OVT if ( driver . ReadStatus ( status ) == DriverStatus :: OK && status . hasFault ()) { if ( status . hasUndervoltage ()) std :: printf ( "VM dropped below UVLO 
 " ); if ( status . hasOvertemperature ()) std :: printf ( "thermal shutdown 
 " ); } max22200 :: FaultStatus per_channel ; // which channel, which fault if ( driver . ReadFaultRegister ( per_channel ) == DriverStatus :: OK && per_channel . hasFault ()) { for ( uint8_t ch = 0 ; ch < 8 ; ++ ch ) { if ( per_channel . hasOvercurrentOnChannel ( ch )) { std :: printf ( "OCP on OUT%u: channel turned off 
 " , ch ); driver . DisableChannel ( ch ); // clear ONCH before turning it on again } } driver . ClearChannelFaults ( per_channel . channelsWithAnyFault ()); // MAX22200A: only these bits } if ( driver . GetLastFaultByte () == max22200 :: StatusReg :: FAULT_BYTE_COMER ) { std :: printf ( "last command byte hit a communication error 
 " ); } Signal Meaning What to do UVM in STATUS VM fell below about 4 V; always set at power-up Reading STATUS clears it OVT in STATUS Thermal shutdown at 145 °C; outputs off until it cools Reading STATUS clears it COMER in STATUS or GetLastFaultByte() = 0x04 The chip ignored a transfer with a wrong clock count Check Transfer() lengths and CS OCP bit in FAULT Output above 1.1 A; that channel turned off Clear ONCH, clear the flag, find the short HHF bit in FAULT HIT current not reached in the HIT time (if hit_current_check_enabled ) Coil resistance, VM, HIT level OLF bit in FAULT Load disconnected (if open_load_detection_enabled ); clears when the output turns on Wiring DPM bit in FAULT No current dip in the HIT phase: the plunger did not move Stuck valve, DPM thresholds FAULT pin low Any unmasked fault above Read STATUS and FAULT STATUS bits OCP, OLF, HHF and DPM summarise FAULT; reading STATUS does not clear them. Mask a fault from the FAULT pin with the ..._masked fields of StatusConfig and WriteStatus() . The fault and state callbacks ( SetFaultCallback() , SetStateChangeCallback() ) are stored but never called by the driver; call them from your own polling code if you use them. Detect plunger movement ¶ // Global DPM settings: search for the dip above 150 mA, dip of at least 40 mA lasting 0.4 ms. if ( driver . ConfigureDpm ( 150.0f , 40.0f , 0.4f ) != DriverStatus :: OK ) return false ; // Per channel: DPM_EN on channels 0 and 1 (low-side only). if ( driver . SetDpmEnabledChannels ( 0b0000'0011 ) != DriverStatus :: OK ) return false ; // A DPM flag in FAULT[7:0] after a HIT means no dip was seen: the plunger did not move. DPM looks for the dip a moving plunger causes in the HIT current. The search starts above the start current and ends at the HIT level or the end of the HIT time; a dip counts when it is deeper than the threshold and longer than the debounce time. The settings are global; DPM_EN is per channel and low-side only. The datasheet asks for a current slope below 700 mA/ms above the start current. ConfigureDpm() converts the debounce with the FMAIN_DIV4 frequency whatever the channels use; use WriteDpmConfig() for other frequencies. Use a register directly ¶ uint32_t cfg0 = 0 ; if ( driver . ReadRegister32 ( max22200 :: RegBank :: CFG_CH0 , cfg0 ) != DriverStatus :: OK ) return false ; // 8-bit access reaches bits [31:24] only: for CFG_CHx that is HFS and HOLD[6:0]. const uint8_t hold_raw = 40 ; // 40 / 127 x IFS return driver . WriteRegister8 ( max22200 :: RegBank :: CFG_CH0 , static_cast < uint8_t > (( cfg0 >> 24 ) & 0x80u ) | hold_raw ) == DriverStatus :: OK ; Banks are max22200::RegBank::STATUS , CFG_CH0 to CFG_CH7 , FAULT and CFG_DPM ; bit positions are in the StatusReg , CfgChReg , FaultReg and CfgDpmReg namespaces. An 8-bit access reaches bits [31:24] only. A raw STATUS write bypasses the driver's cache: call ReadStatus() afterwards. Count transfers ¶ const max22200 :: DriverStatistics s = driver . GetStatistics (); std :: printf ( "%lu transfers, %lu failed (%.1f %% ok) 
 " , static_cast < unsigned long > ( s . total_transfers ), static_cast < unsigned long > ( s . failed_transfers ), static_cast < double > ( s . getSuccessRate ())); Only total_transfers and failed_transfers are counted; fault_events , state_changes and uptime_ms stay 0.

The settings are global; DPM_EN is per channel and low-side only. The datasheet asks for a current slope below 700 mA/ms above the start current. ConfigureDpm() converts the debounce with the FMAIN_DIV4 frequency whatever the channels use; use WriteDpmConfig() for other frequencies.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one call reaches the chip. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one MAX22200 object; its main calls (listed from inc/max22200.hpp) configure channels, switch them, and read faults. Each call becomes the chip's two-phase SPI access: a command byte with CMD high, then 8 or 32 data bits with CMD low. The communication interface (SpiInterface in inc/max22200_spi_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base that forwards those transfers and the ENABLE, CMD and FAULT pins to your class. The platform port is the only code you write. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/max22200.hpp MAX22200 public calls ; inc/max22200_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The three layers ¶ Layer Where You change it when Hardware-agnostic core : MAX22200<SpiType> inc/max22200.hpp , src/max22200.ipp Never, for a new board Communication interface : SpiInterface<Derived> inc/max22200_spi_interface.hpp Never Platform port : your class Your project Once per MCU or board ( Porting ) Everything above the port is the same on ESP32, STM32, a Linux host or the unit-test model. That is how the host tests run the real driver code without hardware. How one call reaches the chip ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant D as MAX22200 core participant P as Your port participant C as MAX22200 chip A->>D: ConfigureChannel(0, cfg) D->>D: check channel, IFS, SRC vs fCHOP D->>D: mA to HIT/HOLD (x 127 / IFS), ms to HIT_T (x fCHOP / 40) D->>P: GpioSet(CMD, ACTIVE) D->>P: Transfer({0x82}, 1 byte) P->>C: CSB low, command byte, CSB high C-->>P: STATUS[7:0] D->>P: GpioSet(CMD, INACTIVE) D->>P: Transfer(4 bytes, LSB first) P->>C: CSB low, CFG_CH0, CSB high D-->>A: DriverStatus::OK Why CRTP ¶ The interface is a class template parameter, not a virtual base class. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable, allocates nothing and needs no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: MAX22200<MySpi> . Code that has to work with several port types takes the driver as a template parameter too. State the driver keeps ¶ The driver holds a reference to your port, never a copy, and a few values in the object: State Why BoardConfig IFS and optional current and duty limits for every unit conversion Cached STATUS ONCH for the 8-bit channel writes, FREQM for HIT-time and duty conversions Last fault byte STATUS[7:0] from the most recent command byte ( GetLastFaultByte() ) DriverStatistics Transfer and failure counters The STATUS cache is refreshed by ReadStatus() , WriteStatus() and Initialize() . If something else writes STATUS (a raw WriteRegister32() , another task), call ReadStatus() before the next EnableChannel() : the 8-bit ONCH write uses the cached mask for the channels you did not name. Errors without exceptions ¶ Every call that touches the chip returns max22200::DriverStatus : Value Meaning OK Done INVALID_PARAMETER Channel above 7, pair above 3, IFS of 0, SRC at 50 kHz or more, a value out of range; nothing is written COMMUNICATION_ERROR Your Transfer() or GpioRead() returned false , or Initialize() saw COMER three times INITIALIZATION_ERROR Your Initialize() or Configure() returned false HARDWARE_FAULT and TIMEOUT exist in the enum but no call returns them. Chip faults (overcurrent, open load) are not errors of the call: read them with ReadStatus() and ReadFaultRegister() . docs.text: Drive modes ¶ What a channel does on its output in each mode, and how the driver turns milliamps, percent and milliseconds into the CFG_CHx register. HIT and HOLD ¶ Every channel runs a two-level sequence each time it is switched on (by ONCH over SPI or by its TRIG pin): a HIT level for the HIT time, to pull a plunger in, then a lower HOLD level until it is switched off. The HOLD time is not programmable; it lasts as long as the channel stays on. stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Off Off --> Hit: ONCHx = 1 or TRIG high Hit --> Hold: HIT time elapsed Hit --> Off: ONCHx = 0 Hold --> Off: ONCHx = 0 or TRIG low Current drive (CDR) ¶ The chip senses the output current internally and chops to hold its peak at the target. CDR is the reset default and works on low-side channels only. HIT and HOLD are 7-bit fractions of the full-scale current IFS (datasheet Table 4): HIT[6:0] or HOLD[6:0] Output 0 Off (high-side switch on, low-side off) 1 to 126 Peak current = value / 127 × IFS 127 Low-side switch fully on, no regulation ChannelConfig::hit_setpoint and hold_setpoint are in milliamps in CDR. The driver writes round(mA × 127 / IFS), and writes 127 for any value at or above IFS. IFS comes from BoardConfig ; with half_full_scale set on a channel the driver uses IFS / 2 for that channel, and the chip doubles the low-side on-resistance to 0.4 Ω. Use HFS for coils that need less than half of IFS: the resolution doubles. The regulated value is the peak. The average current is lower by half the ripple, and the ripple grows as the chopping frequency falls. Voltage drive (VDR) ¶ The chip outputs a fixed-frequency PWM; the current follows from VM and the coil resistance. VDR is the only mode for high-side channels (load to GND). The datasheet (Table 3) defines HIT[6:0] and HOLD[6:0] in VDR as the duty cycle in percent: 0 is off, values from δMIN to δMAX are that duty, 100 and above is fully on, and values between are clamped to δMIN or δMAX. VDR duty is scaled by 127 / 100 in the current driver ChannelConfig::toRegister() writes a VDR percentage as round(percent × 127 / 100), the same scaling it uses for CDR. By Table 3 the chip reads the register as percent, so a requested 40 % runs at 51 %. 0 % and 100 % are exact. Until this is fixed, write the percentage you want × 100 / 127 (40 % → 31.5), or set the field with WriteRegister32() . Chopping frequency ¶ The oscillator runs at 100 kHz ( FREQM = 0, STATUS) or 80 kHz ( FREQM = 1) for the whole chip; each channel divides it with FREQ_CFG ( ChannelConfig::chop_freq , datasheet Table 1): chop_freq FREQ_CFG FREQM = 0 (kHz) FREQM = 1 (kHz) FMAIN_DIV4 00 25 20 FMAIN_DIV3 01 33.3 26.6 FMAIN_DIV2 10 50 40 FMAIN 11 100 80 A higher frequency lowers the current ripple in CDR; a lower one lowers switching losses. The driver reads FREQM from its cached STATUS for every conversion ( StatusConfig::master_clock_80khz ). Duty-cycle limits ¶ In both modes the duty cycle is bounded by δMIN and δMAX (datasheet Table 2). GetDutyLimits() returns them for a channel. Setting δMIN δMAX SRC = 0, FMAIN (100 or 80 kHz) 8 % 92 % SRC = 0, any other divider 4 % 96 % SRC = 1 (below 50 kHz only) 7 % 93 % HIT time ¶ HIT_T is 8 bits (datasheet Table 5): 0 is no HIT phase, 1 to 254 is HIT_T × 40 / fCHOP, 255 is a continuous HIT. hit_time_ms is converted with the channel's fCHOP and rounded; negative values mean continuous. fCHOP (kHz) Step (ms) Longest finite HIT (ms) 20 2 508 25 1.6 406.4 50 0.8 203.2 100 0.4 101.6 The driver computes fCHOP for FMAIN_DIV3 as 33 kHz and 26 kHz, not 33.3 and 26.6, so HIT times on that divider read back about 1 % off. Slew-rate control ¶ slew_rate_control_enabled (SRC) slows the output edges to about 200 ns to cut emissions, and doubles the overcurrent deglitch time. It is low-side only and allowed only below 50 kHz: ConfigureChannel() returns INVALID_PARAMETER for SRC at 50 kHz or more. Use HFS for coils that need less than half of IFS: the resolution doubles. The regulated value is the peak. The average current is lower by half the ripple, and the ripple grows as the chopping frequency falls.
docs.title: Current drive (CDR)

docs.text: The chip outputs a fixed-frequency PWM; the current follows from VM and the coil resistance. VDR is the only mode for high-side channels (load to GND). The datasheet (Table 3) defines HIT[6:0] and HOLD[6:0] in VDR as the duty cycle in percent: 0 is off, values from δMIN to δMAX are that duty, 100 and above is fully on, and values between are clamped to δMIN or δMAX. VDR duty is scaled by 127 / 100 in the current driver ChannelConfig::toRegister() writes a VDR percentage as round(percent × 127 / 100), the same scaling it uses for CDR. By Table 3 the chip reads the register as percent, so a requested 40 % runs at 51 %. 0 % and 100 % are exact. Until this is fixed, write the percentage you want × 100 / 127 (40 % → 31.5), or set the field with WriteRegister32() .
docs.title: Voltage drive (VDR)

docs.text: The oscillator runs at 100 kHz ( FREQM = 0, STATUS) or 80 kHz ( FREQM = 1) for the whole chip; each channel divides it with FREQ_CFG ( ChannelConfig::chop_freq , datasheet Table 1): chop_freq FREQ_CFG FREQM = 0 (kHz) FREQM = 1 (kHz) FMAIN_DIV4 00 25 20 FMAIN_DIV3 01 33.3 26.6 FMAIN_DIV2 10 50 40 FMAIN 11 100 80 A higher frequency lowers the current ripple in CDR; a lower one lowers switching losses. The driver reads FREQM from its cached STATUS for every conversion ( StatusConfig::master_clock_80khz ).
docs.title: Chopping frequency

docs.text: In both modes the duty cycle is bounded by δMIN and δMAX (datasheet Table 2). GetDutyLimits() returns them for a channel. Setting δMIN δMAX SRC = 0, FMAIN (100 or 80 kHz) 8 % 92 % SRC = 0, any other divider 4 % 96 % SRC = 1 (below 50 kHz only) 7 % 93 %
docs.title: Duty-cycle limits

docs.text: HIT_T is 8 bits (datasheet Table 5): 0 is no HIT phase, 1 to 254 is HIT_T × 40 / fCHOP, 255 is a continuous HIT. hit_time_ms is converted with the channel's fCHOP and rounded; negative values mean continuous. fCHOP (kHz) Step (ms) Longest finite HIT (ms) 20 2 508 25 1.6 406.4 50 0.8 203.2 100 0.4 101.6 The driver computes fCHOP for FMAIN_DIV3 as 33 kHz and 26 kHz, not 33.3 and 26.6, so HIT times on that divider read back about 1 % off.

docs.text: slew_rate_control_enabled (SRC) slows the output edges to about 200 ns to cut emissions, and doubles the overcurrent deglitch time. It is low-side only and allowed only below 50 kHz: ConfigureChannel() returns INVALID_PARAMETER for SRC at 50 kHz or more.

docs.text: Hardware ¶ What to connect between your MCU and a MAX22200, with which bus settings and timing, and what the supply and outputs need. All values here come from the MAX22200 datasheet (19-100531, Rev. 1, 3/25). Pin numbers are for the 32-pin TQFN; when they disagree with a board's schematic, the schematic wins. Host interface pins ¶ Pin Direction Notes CSB (3) in SPI chip select, active low; internal pull-up current SCK (5) in Data in on the rising edge, out on the falling edge; internal pull-down SDI (6) in SPI data from the MCU SDO (7) out, open drain Needs an external pull-up; its RC sets the highest usable clock CMD (2) in High: the transfer writes the Command Register. Low: data. Internal pull-down ENABLE (21) in High enables the chip, low is sleep; 1.5 MΩ internal pull-down FAULT (1) out, open drain Low while an unmasked fault is present; needs a pull-up TRIGA (8) in Trigger for channels 0, 2, 4, 6 when their TRGnSPI bit is set; pull-down TRIGB (17) in Trigger for channels 1, 3, 5, 7; pull-down The driver drives ENABLE and CMD and reads FAULT through your port by name ( max22200::CtrlPin ) and state ( GpioSignal::ACTIVE / INACTIVE ). ENABLE and CMD are active high, FAULT is active low; your port maps each state to a level. TRIGA and TRIGB are not used by the driver: drive them from your own GPIOs or leave them low. There is no separate logic supply. Logic inputs switch at 1.2 V (V IH , min) and 0.65 V (V IL , max) and tolerate 6 V, so 1.8 V, 3.3 V and 5 V MCUs connect directly. ENABLE switches at 0.9 V / 0.6 V and is rated to VM. Output and power pins ¶ Pin What it is Connect OUT0 to OUT7 Half-bridge outputs (31, 30, 27, 26, 10, 11, 14, 15) Low side: load to VM. High side: load to GND VM Supply (9, 12, 13, 16, 25, 28, 29, 32) Two 0.1 µF ceramics at pins 12/13 and 28/29, plus 10 µF electrolytic IREF (18) Current reference 15 kΩ to 100 kΩ to GND; sets IFS for CDR V18 (20) 1.8 V internal regulator 2.2 µF ceramic to GND VCP (24) Charge-pump output 1 µF, 5 V or more, to VM CFP , CFN (23, 22) Charge-pump flying capacitor 22 nF, VM-rated, between them GND , EP Signal ground (4, 19), power ground pad Board ground; vias under the pad for heat Pairs 0-1, 2-3, 4-5 and 6-7 can be wired in parallel (outputs tied together) for twice the current, or used as a full bridge across a motor or latching valve. Both are set in STATUS; see API guide . Full-scale current (IREF) ¶ In CDR the HIT and HOLD currents are fractions of a full-scale current set by RREF: I FS = K FS × 1 V / R REF , with K FS = 15 000 (HFS = 0) or 7 500 (HFS = 1, per channel). RREF (kΩ) IFS, HFS = 0 (mA) IFS, HFS = 1 (mA) 15 1000 500 30 500 250 50 300 150 100 150 75 Pass RREF to the driver with BoardConfig(rref_kohm, false) ; it computes IFS for HFS = 0 and halves it for any channel with half_full_scale set. CDR accuracy is ±6 % from 71 % to 100 % of IFS and widens to ±25 % at 5 % to 10 % (IFS = 1 A, 1 % RREF). Bus settings ¶ Setting Value Mode 0 (CPOL = 0, CPHA = 0), MSB first Clock Up to 10 MHz (t CLK ≥ 100 ns); 5 MHz when daisy-chained; start at 1 MHz Frame 8 bits with CMD high (command), then 8 or 32 bits with CMD low (data) Chip select Low for the whole frame; high at least 30 ns between frames 32-bit byte order Write: LSB byte first on SDI. Read: MSB byte first on SDO The driver supports one chip per bus; it does not build daisy-chained frames. It does not wait t WU : give the chip 2.5 ms after Initialize() before you expect an output to switch. Power ¶ Quantity Value VM operating range 4.5 V to 36 V (absolute maximum 40 V) Sleep current, ENABLE low ≤ 11 µA ACTIVE = 0 current 200 µA typical, 400 µA maximum Quiescent, all channels off / CDR on, no load 2.5 mA / 5.2 mA typical VM undervoltage lockout 4 V typical rising (3.75 V to 4.25 V), 0.12 V hysteresis At power-up every register is at its default, ACTIVE is 0 and the UVM flag is set, so FAULT is low until the first STATUS read. A VM dip below UVLO three-states the outputs but keeps the registers; only a dip that takes V18 below its reset threshold (about 1 V) resets them. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 12+ or a current MSVC. No RTOS, heap or exceptions: every call returns a max22200::DriverStatus and never throws. Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-max22200-driver.git external/hf-max22200-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-max22200-driver Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-max22200-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf::max22200 ) hf::max22200 is an alias of the hf_max22200 interface target. It carries the include directories ( inc/ and the generated version header) and requires C++20 ( cxx_std_20 ), so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect HF_MAX22200_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF Adds -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic to targets that link the driver HF_MAX22200_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host unit tests in tests/ ( Testing and CI ) Use the source tree, not cmake --install The install rules copy inc/ but not src/max22200.ipp , which max22200.hpp includes. Until that is fixed, consume the driver with add_subdirectory() or the ESP-IDF component. ESP-IDF ¶ The ESP-IDF component wrapper is examples/esp32/components/hf_max22200/ . Copy that folder into your project's components/ (or point EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at it) and set the HF_MAX22200_ROOT cache variable to the driver checkout; the wrapper stops with a clear message when the path is wrong. Your component then declares REQUIRES hf_max22200 . Without CMake ¶ Add inc/ to the include path and generate max22200_version.h from inc/max22200_version.h.in once (replace the four @...@ fields with the version). max22200.hpp includes src/max22200.ipp by relative path, so keep inc/ and src/ side by side. How the build is organised ¶ File Role cmake/hf_max22200_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, version: the single source of truth CMakeLists.txt Interface library for host builds and CI examples/esp32/components/hf_max22200/CMakeLists.txt ESP-IDF component over the same settings The version is set once in the settings file and written into max22200_version.h at configure time. Read it at run time: const char * v = max22200 :: MAX22200 < MySpi >:: GetDriverVersion (); // "1.0.0" Next ¶ Quickstart wires the chip and drives a solenoid; Porting writes the SPI interface for your MCU.

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the SPI interface. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls eight methods on a class you derive from max22200::SpiInterface<Self> (in inc/max22200_spi_interface.hpp ). The base class uses CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions, no vtable and nothing to allocate. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one MAX22200 object; its main calls (listed from inc/max22200.hpp) configure channels, switch them, and read faults. Each call becomes the chip's two-phase SPI access: a command byte with CMD high, then 8 or 32 data bits with CMD low. The communication interface (SpiInterface in inc/max22200_spi_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base that forwards those transfers and the ENABLE, CMD and FAULT pins to your class. The platform port is the only code you write. Below it is the hardware. Drawn from: inc/max22200.hpp MAX22200 public calls ; inc/max22200_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method Contract Initialize() Bring the SPI peripheral and the GPIOs up. Called first by the driver's Initialize() Configure(hz, mode, msb_first) Called with 10 MHz, mode 0, true . Apply it, or keep a lower clock Transfer(tx, rx, len) One blocking full-duplex transaction of len bytes (1 or 4), CS low for all of it GpioSet(pin, signal) Drive ENABLE or CMD : ACTIVE is high for both GpioRead(pin, signal) Read FAULT : low is ACTIVE . Return false if the pin is not wired DelayUs(us) Block for at least that long (the 0.5 ms enable time) SetChipSelect(state) Required by the base class; the driver does not call it IsReady() Required by the base class; the driver does not call it The port ¶ my_spi.hpp class MySpi : public max22200 :: SpiInterface < MySpi > { public : // Board wiring: ENABLE and CMD are MCU outputs, FAULT is an input with a pull-up. static constexpr int kEnablePin = 4 ; static constexpr int kCmdPin = 5 ; static constexpr int kFaultPin = 6 ; // Cap the clock: 1 MHz for bring-up, at most 10 MHz alone or 5 MHz in a daisy chain. explicit MySpi ( uint32_t max_clock_hz = 10000000 ) : max_clock_hz_ ( max_clock_hz ) {} bool Initialize () { return true ; } // The driver calls this once from Initialize(): 10 MHz, mode 0, MSB first. bool Configure ( uint32_t speed_hz , uint8_t mode , bool msb_first ) { const uint32_t hz = speed_hz < max_clock_hz_ ? speed_hz : max_clock_hz_ ; return mode == 0 && msb_first && platform_spi_init ( hz , mode ); } bool IsReady () const { return true ; } // One blocking, full-duplex transaction: CS low, `length` bytes, CS high, then return. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t length ) { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , length ); } void SetChipSelect ( bool ) {} // Transfer() owns CS; the driver never calls this void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // ENABLE and CMD are active high, FAULT is active low (open drain). void GpioSet ( max22200 :: CtrlPin pin , max22200 :: GpioSignal signal ) { const bool high = signal == max22200 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; if ( pin == max22200 :: CtrlPin :: ENABLE ) platform_gpio_write ( kEnablePin , high ); if ( pin == max22200 :: CtrlPin :: CMD ) platform_gpio_write ( kCmdPin , high ); } bool GpioRead ( max22200 :: CtrlPin pin , max22200 :: GpioSignal & signal ) { if ( pin != max22200 :: CtrlPin :: FAULT ) return false ; signal = platform_gpio_read ( kFaultPin ) ? max22200 :: GpioSignal :: INACTIVE : max22200 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ; return true ; } private : uint32_t max_clock_hz_ ; }; Rules the transfer must follow: SPI mode 0 , MSB first, at most 10 MHz (5 MHz with daisy-chained parts on the bus). One transaction per call. CS goes low before the first byte and high after the last; never split a call, never merge two. The chip counts clocks and flags a communication error on a wrong count. Return after CS is high. The driver raises CMD, calls Transfer() for the command byte and lowers CMD as soon as it returns. CMD must still be high at the CS rising edge, so a queued or DMA transfer that returns early breaks every access. Fill rx . The driver reads the fault byte and register values from it. Return false only for a bus failure. The driver turns it into COMMUNICATION_ERROR . Pin levels ¶ Pin (MCU side) ACTIVE level At power-up ENABLE (output) high low: chip asleep CMD (output) high low FAULT (input, pull-up) low low until the first STATUS read (UVM) A board with an inverting buffer flips the level in your GpioSet() or GpioRead() ; the driver only deals in ACTIVE and INACTIVE . If ENABLE is tied high on your board, ignore it in GpioSet() ; if FAULT is not wired, return false from GpioRead() and poll ReadStatus() instead. Reference implementation ¶ The ESP32 examples use esp32_max22200_bus.hpp : an ESP-IDF spi_master port with spi_device_transmit() (blocking, CS handled by the peripheral), esp_rom_delay_us() and GPIOs for ENABLE, CMD, FAULT, TRIGA and TRIGB. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the port on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over it. Call Initialize() . OK proves the command and data phases work: the driver reads STATUS, writes it and reads it back. Write a channel with ConfigureChannel() , read it with ReadRegister32() and compare the raw values ( SPI protocol decodes them). Watch GetStatistics() : failed_transfers should stay at zero. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each MAX22200 one owner task, or guard every call on a driver object (and its port) with one mutex. Other devices can share the SPI bus: the MAX22200 only sees transfers with its own CS, and its command stays in force between them, so locking the bus inside each Transfer() call is enough.

Channel 0: low-side CDR, 400 mA for 20 ms to pull in, then 150 mA to hold. const auto valve = max22200 :: ChannelConfig :: makeSolenoidCdr ( 400.0f , 150.0f , 20.0f ); if ( driver . docs.text: SPI protocol ¶ How the MAX22200's two-phase SPI access works, byte by byte, and how to read it on a logic analyser or in a log. Every register access is two SPI transactions: the 8-bit Command Register with CMD high, then the data with CMD low. The driver's private writeCommandRegister() and readData32() / writeData32() / readData8() / writeData8() do exactly this; the references are datasheet Table 9 and Figures 7 and 10 to 13. Command byte ¶ Bit Name Meaning 7 RB/W 0 = read, 1 = write 6:5 RFU Write 0 4:1 A_BNK Register: 0x00 STATUS, 0x01 to 0x08 CFG_CH0 to CFG_CH7, 0x09 FAULT, 0x0A CFG_DPM 0 8bit/n32bits 1 = the data phase is 8 bits (bits [31:24] only), 0 = 32 bits max22200::CommandReg::build(bank, write, mode8) builds it. The bytes you will see most: Byte Access 0x00 / 0x80 Read / write STATUS, 32 bits 0x81 Write STATUS[31:24] (ONCH), 8 bits: channel on/off 0x02 / 0x82 Read / write CFG_CH0, 32 bits (CFG_CHn: 0x02 + 2n ) 0x12 Read FAULT, 32 bits 0x14 / 0x94 Read / write CFG_DPM While CMD is high the chip shifts STATUS[7:0], the fault flag byte, out on SDO. 0x04 there is COMER: the chip rejected the previous transfer. The driver keeps the byte; read it with GetLastFaultByte() . The command stays in force: every following CMD-low transfer is of the same type until a new command byte. The driver always sends a command before each data phase, so it never depends on this. Data phase ¶ Access SDI (host to chip) SDO (chip to host) Write, 32 bits DATAIN[7:0], [15:8], [23:16], [31:24] STATUS[7:0], command echo, 0x00 , 0x00 Read, 32 bits Don't care (FAULT on MAX22200A: clear mask) DATA[31:24], [23:16], [15:8], [7:0] Write, 8 bits DATAIN[31:24] STATUS[7:0] Read, 8 bits Don't care DATA[31:24] 32-bit writes go least significant byte first and 32-bit reads come most significant byte first; this is what the datasheet's figures show, and the driver follows it. Within each byte, bits are MSB first. The chip counts clocks on writes: a 32-bit write checks the first 32, then every 8; an 8-bit write checks every 8. A wrong count is a communication error: the transfer is ignored and COMER sets (FAULT goes low only if M_COMF is 0; it is 1 after reset and Initialize() keeps it). Selective clear on read (MAX22200A) ¶ Reading FAULT on the MAX22200A clears only the bits whose SDI bit is high during the read. The SDI bytes line up with the SDO bytes: first OCP, then HHF, OLF, DPM. To clear the overcurrent flag of OUT4 alone, send 0x10 0x00 0x00 0x00 while reading. ClearChannelFaults(mask) sends the mask in all four bytes; ReadFaultRegisterSelectiveClear() takes one mask per fault type. The MAX22200 ignores SDI and clears every bit. Decoding a log ¶ The ESP32 port prints every transfer with ESP32_MAX22200_ENABLE_DETAILED_SPI_LOGGING . Two examples: Log Meaning SPI(1) TX: 82 RX: 03 , then SPI(4) TX: 00 06 50 28 RX: 03 82 00 00 Write CFG_CH0 = 0x28500600 ; fault byte 0x03 (ACTIVE, UVM), command echoed SPI(1) TX: 00 RX: 03 , then SPI(4) TX: 00 00 00 00 RX: 00 04 00 03 Read STATUS = 0x00040003 : no channel on, M_COMF set, ACTIVE = 1, UVM = 1 0x28500600 decodes as HOLD = 0x28 (40 / 127 of IFS), HIT = 0x50 (80 / 127), HIT_T = 6 (6 × 40 / 25 kHz = 9.6 ms) and CDR, low side, FREQ_CFG = 00. A requested 10 ms reads back as 9.6 ms: the HIT time is an 8-bit count of 40 chopping periods. When you test a write, compare the raw register value you wrote with the one you read; the values in milliamps and milliseconds are quantised. docs.text: Bit Name Meaning 7 RB/W 0 = read, 1 = write 6:5 RFU Write 0 4:1 A_BNK Register: 0x00 STATUS, 0x01 to 0x08 CFG_CH0 to CFG_CH7, 0x09 FAULT, 0x0A CFG_DPM 0 8bit/n32bits 1 = the data phase is 8 bits (bits [31:24] only), 0 = 32 bits max22200::CommandReg::build(bank, write, mode8) builds it. The bytes you will see most: Byte Access 0x00 / 0x80 Read / write STATUS, 32 bits 0x81 Write STATUS[31:24] (ONCH), 8 bits: channel on/off 0x02 / 0x82 Read / write CFG_CH0, 32 bits (CFG_CHn: 0x02 + 2n ) 0x12 Read FAULT, 32 bits 0x14 / 0x94 Read / write CFG_DPM While CMD is high the chip shifts STATUS[7:0], the fault flag byte, out on SDO. 0x04 there is COMER: the chip rejected the previous transfer. The driver keeps the byte; read it with GetLastFaultByte() . The command stays in force: every following CMD-low transfer is of the same type until a new command byte. The driver always sends a command before each data phase, so it never depends on this.
docs.title: Command byte

docs.text: Access SDI (host to chip) SDO (chip to host) Write, 32 bits DATAIN[7:0], [15:8], [23:16], [31:24] STATUS[7:0], command echo, 0x00 , 0x00 Read, 32 bits Don't care (FAULT on MAX22200A: clear mask) DATA[31:24], [23:16], [15:8], [7:0] Write, 8 bits DATAIN[31:24] STATUS[7:0] Read, 8 bits Don't care DATA[31:24] 32-bit writes go least significant byte first and 32-bit reads come most significant byte first; this is what the datasheet's figures show, and the driver follows it. Within each byte, bits are MSB first. The chip counts clocks on writes: a 32-bit write checks the first 32, then every 8; an 8-bit write checks every 8. A wrong count is a communication error: the transfer is ignored and COMER sets (FAULT goes low only if M_COMF is 0; it is 1 after reset and Initialize() keeps it).
docs.title: Data phase

docs.text: Reading FAULT on the MAX22200A clears only the bits whose SDI bit is high during the read. The SDI bytes line up with the SDO bytes: first OCP, then HHF, OLF, DPM. To clear the overcurrent flag of OUT4 alone, send 0x10 0x00 0x00 0x00 while reading. ClearChannelFaults(mask) sends the mask in all four bytes; ReadFaultRegisterSelectiveClear() takes one mask per fault type. The MAX22200 ignores SDI and clears every bit.
docs.title: Selective clear on read (MAX22200A)

docs.text: The ESP32 port prints every transfer with ESP32_MAX22200_ENABLE_DETAILED_SPI_LOGGING . Two examples: Log Meaning SPI(1) TX: 82 RX: 03 , then SPI(4) TX: 00 06 50 28 RX: 03 82 00 00 Write CFG_CH0 = 0x28500600 ; fault byte 0x03 (ACTIVE, UVM), command echoed SPI(1) TX: 00 RX: 03 , then SPI(4) TX: 00 00 00 00 RX: 00 04 00 03 Read STATUS = 0x00040003 : no channel on, M_COMF set, ACTIVE = 1, UVM = 1 0x28500600 decodes as HOLD = 0x28 (40 / 127 of IFS), HIT = 0x50 (80 / 127), HIT_T = 6 (6 × 40 / 25 kHz = 9.6 ms) and CDR, low side, FREQ_CFG = 00. A requested 10 ms reads back as 9.6 ms: the HIT time is an 8-bit count of 40 chopping periods. When you test a write, compare the raw register value you wrote with the one you read; the values in milliamps and milliseconds are quantised.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see while bringing up a MAX22200, their causes and the fix for each. Start with the cheapest checks: the return value of the failing call, GetLastFaultByte() and a raw STATUS read. They tell bus problems (no reply, COMER) apart from chip problems (the chip answers but reports a fault). The max22200_diagnostic example prints all three, plus a CFG_CH0 round trip, with every SPI byte. Start-up ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Initialize() returns INITIALIZATION_ERROR Your port's Initialize() or Configure() returned false Check the port: SPI host, pins, mode 0 accepted Initialize() returns COMMUNICATION_ERROR Transfer() failed, or the chip answered COMER ( 0x04 ) three times CMD wiring and level; Transfer() blocking until CS is high; one call, one CS frame Every read is 0xFF or 0x00 SDO not pulled up, ENABLE low, VM off or below 4.5 V Pull-up on SDO, ENABLE trace, VM at the chip pins Initialize() is OK but STATUS reads ACTIVE = 0 or UVM = 1 VM sagging below UVLO, or V18 not settled Check VM under load, the 2.2 µF on V18, the charge-pump parts; write ACTIVE again after the supply is stable STATUS has impossible values (reserved CMxy = 11, ONCH set at boot) The chip kept its registers through an MCU reset Registers reset only when V18 falls below about 1 V: power-cycle VM Channels ¶ Symptom Cause Fix Channel is on in ONCH but the output does not switch Less than 2.5 ms (t WU ) since ACTIVE = 1, or ACTIVE = 0 Wait after Initialize() ; check StatusConfig::active Low-side channel does nothing, high side works (or the reverse) The load is wired for the other side Low side: load to VM. High side: load to GND, VDR only ConfigureChannel() returns INVALID_PARAMETER IFS is 0, SRC at 50 kHz or more, or channel above 7 SetBoardConfig() , a lower chop_freq , the channel number Drive mode or side does not change A channel is on, or TRIGA / TRIGB is high Switch every channel off and hold both TRIG pins low first Current is off by a constant factor IFS does not match RREF, or BoardConfig(r, true) and half_full_scale both set BoardConfig(rref_kohm, false) with the real RREF VDR duty is higher than requested The driver scales VDR percent by 127 / 100 See Drive modes HIT time reads back shorter or longer HIT_T is an 8-bit count of 40 chopping periods Expected; compare raw register values Another channel turns off when you enable one STATUS was written outside the driver; the ONCH cache is stale ReadStatus() after any raw STATUS write Faults ¶ Symptom Cause Fix FAULT low right after power-up UVM is set at every power-up Initialize() reads STATUS, which clears it OCP on a channel Output above 1.1 A: a short, or a coil with too low resistance in VDR Clear ONCH, read FAULT to clear the flag, fix the load HHF on a channel HIT current not reached within the HIT time VM too low for the coil resistance, HIT too high, HIT time too short OLF on a channel Load disconnected, with open_load_detection_enabled set Wiring; the flag clears when the output turns on DPM on every cycle No dip seen: the plunger is stuck, or the thresholds are too strict Hold the plunger to compare; tune with c21_dpm_tuning_test DPM never fires, even with the plunger held Current slope above 700 mA/ms above the start current, or the start current above the dip Set the start current just below the expected dip; check the slope on a scope ClearChannelFaults() clears other channels too The part is a MAX22200, not a MAX22200A Expected: the MAX22200 clears every flag on any FAULT read A DPM flag means no dip was revealed, so a healthy valve produces no DPM flags. To check that detection works, hold the plunger still during one cycle: the flag should set for that cycle.

Your application talks to one MAX22200 object; its main calls (listed from inc/max22200.hpp) configure channels, switch them, and read faults.
